_about: The keying rules of the Jesup workspace: the Americanist notation The Chukchee prints, as keying_spec.md §2-3 state it, which remains their owner. Read by harness/keying.py, which lays a text's own config/keying.json over this one key by key. Moved byte for byte from the module constants that held them (detectors, normalize, validate); `harness corpus rules` shows the effective table for a text and which tier set each entry.
_shape: Every table maps a key to what it is. inventory and lookalikes: a codepoint to its name. tier1_traps: a trap to the glyph it displaces. lookalike_*: a trap to its message, in 'X traps Y' idiom. mark_license and orthographic_bases: a mark to {base: why}. detectors: a switch (keying.DETECTORS) to what it catches; present is on. tier2_scripts: an ISO 15924 code to why no token in it is Tier-1. prose_alphabet: a script to the letters of its prose, against which any other letter or mark in a token of that script is notation (or an error) — an exclusion list, so a novel glyph stays loud. folds: what an OCR emits for a sort (a letter, or a letter and its marks, in NFD) to what the editor identified it as, applied wherever text enters a store; an identity, so only ever the editor's.

detectors.word_medial_caps: a full-height A E I L inside a word: the small capitals ɪ ᴇ ʟ ᴀ keyed as capitals
detectors.dot_above_g: g+U+0307 or U+0121 where the notation prints g̣, dot below
detectors.suffix_mark_drop: a bare g before -ɪ/-ɪn/-ɪt, where g̣ is the measured reading (§5.1)
detectors.apostrophe_unlicensed: U+0027 inside a token bearing notation: a mistyped stress ˊ (§2.1), so the token is Tier-1

tier2_scripts.Cyrl: Russian is Tier-2 prose in a Jesup volume (§2.7): no Cyrillic token is evidence about the notation
